subject: maths
title: Year 5 Adding and Subtracting Fractions
seo_title: Year 5 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets: Free Maths with Answer Key (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same or related denominators, using different strategies
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting fractions, aligned to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M5N05): same and related denominators, bar models, answers as mixed numerals, mixed numerals and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, great for NAPLAN practice.
key_big: Make the parts the same size, then add or subtract the numerators. The denominator stays the same.
key_sub: 1/4 + 3/8 = 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8, not 4/12. If the answer is more than 1, write it as a mixed numeral: 6/5 = 1 1/5.
body_html:
Same denominator: add the numerators

The denominator tells you the size of the parts. The numerator tells you how many parts. When the denominators are the same, the parts are the same size, so you just add or subtract the numerators. The denominator stays the same.

Example

67 − 27 = ?

The denominators are the same. Subtract the numerators: 6 − 2 = 4. The denominator stays 7.

Answer: 47

Related denominators: one is a multiple of the other

Quarters and eighths are different sizes. 8 is a multiple of 4, so change the quarters into eighths. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number.

Example

14 + 38 = ?

4 × 2 = 8, so 14 = 28. Add the numerators: 28 + 38 = 58.

Answer: 58

Example

56 − 13 = ?

6 is a multiple of 3, so 13 = 26. 56 − 26 = 36. This is the same as 12.

Answer: 36 = 12

Answers greater than 1

If the numerator is bigger than the denominator, the answer is an improper fraction. Change it to a mixed numeral: divide the numerator by the denominator.

Example

25 + 45 = ?

25 + 45 = 65. 6 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 1, so 65 = 1 15.

Answer: 1 15

Mixed numerals

Add or subtract the fractions, then the whole numbers. If the fractions make more than 1, add 1 more whole. If the first fraction is too small to subtract from, rename 1 whole.

CalculationFractionsWhole numbersAnswer
1 12 + 2 3424 + 34 = 54 = 1 141 + 2 + 1 = 44 14
3 − 38rename: 3 = 2 88, 88 − 38 = 5822 58
5 14 − 2 58rename: 4 108 − 2 58, 108 − 58 = 584 − 2 = 22 58
Example

3 − 38 = ?

Rename 1 whole as 88: 3 = 2 88. Then 88 − 38 = 58.

Answer: 2 58

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
27 + 37 = 514 (adding the denominators)Keep the denominator: 57
14 + 38 = 48 (changing the denominator but not the numerator)Multiply the numerator too: 14 = 28, so the total is 58
75 = 2 25 (one whole too many)7 ÷ 5 = 1 remainder 2, so 75 = 1 25
3 − 38 = 3 38 (writing the numbers side by side)Rename 1 whole: 2 88 − 38 = 2 58

faq.q: What fractions do Year 5 students add and subtract in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Fractions with the same denominator, and fractions with related denominators, where one denominator is a multiple of the other, such as 1/4 + 3/8 or 5/6 − 1/3 (AC9M5N05). Answers greater than 1 are written as mixed numerals.

faq.q: How do you teach adding fractions with different denominators in Year 5?
faq.a: Start with a bar model. Show that 1/4 is the same as 2/8, so 1/4 + 3/8 becomes 2/8 + 3/8 = 5/8. Then practise changing one fraction by multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number.

faq.q: How do you subtract a fraction from a whole number?
faq.a: Rename 1 whole as a fraction with the same denominator. For 3 − 3/8, write 3 as 2 8/8, then 8/8 − 3/8 = 5/8, so the answer is 2 5/8. A common mistake is to write 3 3/8.

faq.q: Are fractions on the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test?
faq.a: NAPLAN numeracy is based on the Australian Curriculum, so Year 5 students can meet fraction questions in March. Practising same and related denominators, mixed numerals and word problems helps students prepare.

items.q: On a school excursion, a class walks 2 12 km along a bush track and 1 34 km back to the bus. How far do they walk altogether?
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 24. Add the fractions: 24 + 34 = 54. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 54 is an improper fraction: 54 = 1 14. 3 + 1 14 = 4 14. The answer is 4 14 km.

items.q: A movie lasts 1 12 hours. Mia has watched 34 of an hour of it. How much of the movie is left to watch?
c: 34 of an hour
items.e: 4 is a multiple of 2, so use 4 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 12 = 24. 24 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 1 24 = 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. The answer is 34 of an hour. (That is 45 minutes.)

items.q: Matilda eats 29 of a block of chocolate after lunch and 13 of the block after dinner. How much of the block does she eat?
items.e: 9 is a multiple of 3, so use 9 as the denominator. Write the equivalent fraction: 13 = 39. Add the numerators: 29 + 39 = 59. The answer is 59.

items.q: Lachlan works out 14 + 18 and gets 212. Which is true?
c: He is wrong. It is 28
He is wrong. It is 132
He is wrong. It is 38
items.e: Lachlan added the numerators and the denominators. Quarters and eighths are different sizes, so use eighths: 14 = 28, and 28 + 18 = 38. The answer is 38.

items.q: Which pair of fractions has a total of 1?
c: 35 and 310
56 and 13
12 and 38
23 and 26
items.e: 23 = 46, and 46 + 26 = 66 = 1, so 23 and 26 is correct. The other totals are 910, 78 and 1 16.

items.q: A 1 L jug has 38 L of orange juice and 14 L of pineapple juice in it. How much more can it hold?
items.e: 1 L = 88 L. In it now: 38 + 14 = 38 + 28 = 58 L. Space left: 88 − 58 = 38 L.
